summary.headline: Western Carriers Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose to Rs 449 crore from Rs 440 crore, with total TEUs up over 10% YoY.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 449 crore versus Rs 440 crore a year earlier, and said business volumes grew over 10% YoY despite export headwinds. Container volume in the quarter was 59,343 TEUs, of which 28,933 were domestic and 30,410 were EXIM, about 1,082 more than the prior quarter's 58,261. The company started operations at the GCD Yard general goods terminal at Kolkata Port in early September, with phase one fully operational and incremental volumes expected from Q3. On margins, an analyst noted the decline from high single digits to around 4-5%, and management attributed it to operational excellence efforts amid unpredictable conditions; the call did not quantify margins. Several answers were vague or garbled in the transcript, so the figures above are the ones stated clearly.

about 1,082 TEUs more than the prior quarter's 58,261

segments.name: Domestic container / multimodal
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes are growing and management expects strong domestic performance in coming quarters. An analyst cited about 34% growth in domestic volumes in H1, with the domestic share rising from 37% to 45%; management did not confirm these figures. The company has added many MSME customers at Morbi.

segments.name: EXIM
segments.commentary: EXIM volumes are under pressure from the West Asia crisis and trade headwinds. The company is not yet handling EXIM cargo at its multimodal logistics parks, which are domestic-only for now.

segments.name: Kolkata GCD Yard (general goods terminal)
segments.commentary: Acquired and inaugurated at SMP Port Trust, Kolkata in September 2026, opposite the Calcutta Port gates. Phase one is operational and incremental volumes are expected from Q3.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of strong domestic volumes in coming quarters and expects stronger performance in EXIM, domestic and allied logistics services.
Management says it sees continued opportunities for revenue growth and margin improvement as market conditions evolve, without quantifying targets.
The Vedanta multimodal contract has about two to two and a half years remaining; management said there are no further updates on extension.
capex_capacity: GCD Yard at Kolkata Port (SMP Port Trust) acquired and inaugurated in September 2026, phase one operational, incremental volumes expected from Q3.
Rail services continue to expand to multiple terminals: CMLK (North), Whitefield/Bangalore (South), Kolkata (East) and Guwahati (Northeast).
Management is building rail linkage and storage capabilities; no capex amount was disclosed.
demand_pricing: Demand is broad-based across customers, sectors and geographies, according to management.
Some global signals are turning positive, with expectations of global business returning toward normalcy.
The West Asia crisis is creating uncertainty; management is monitoring it.
Management said margin pressure is linked to unpredictable conditions, and that cost increases are passed through to customers either directly or with a lag; the answer was unclear.
Partner Concord (government-owned) is a supplier; the cost-absorption question was left open for discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days worse than expected in H1 FY27, and what is the receivable-days target for end FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has put in place programmes to reduce receivables and cited recovery after July floods in Gujarat and Maharashtra. No receivable-days figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why have operating margins fallen from high single digits to 4-5%, and how will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the pressure to erratic, unpredictable conditions and said it is improving operational excellence. The answer on pass-through of costs and diesel was unclear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current rail share of the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a clear figure; the answer was garbled in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic share shifting from metals and mining customers to non-metal customers, and how does that affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-metal business is about 45% of the mix and gave no target for the coming years. It said Kolkata is being used to run the supply chain for tiles and ceramics.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vedanta contract be extended, given it may end by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No further updates. Multimodal contracts usually run three to four years; about two to two and a half years remain on this one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the partnership with Concord, and does Concord compete at its Valiya terminal?
qa_highlights.answer: Concord is a principal partner and supplier, not a competitor; the two work together. Management said the Concord cost-absorption question is still under discussion.

risks_watch: EXIM volume pressure from the West Asia crisis and trade headwinds; the company has not yet started EXIM business at its multimodal logistics parks.
Margin compression, with no quantified recovery path in the call.
Receivable days were worse than expected in H1 FY27; no end-FY27 target was given.
Vedanta contract has about two to two and a half years left, and the extension is not confirmed.
Kolkata GCD Yard needs to deliver the incremental volumes expected from Q3.
Cost absorption with Concord (government-owned partner) is unresolved.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic growth and the Kolkata expansion, but cautious on EXIM and margins. Management gave no quantified guidance, and several answers were vague or unclear.
key_quotes: Despite stable volumes there remain certain issues in exemplary.
Resilience does not always require higher inventory across the network.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic growth and the Kolkata GCD Yard, but cautious on EXIM, margins and receivables; analysts pressed on margin recovery, receivable days, rail share and the Vedanta contract, and several answers were vague.

quality.why: Management says business volumes grew over 10% YoY, but reported revenue from operations rose only about 2% (Rs 449 crore vs Rs 440 crore), with EXIM under pressure and domestic growth only partly confirmed; the brief names no one-off items and gives no price/mix split, so the growth driver is not clearly stated.
